transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Hello, this is calling from our company. Is this a good time to talk about your account?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.message:
*sighs heavily, voice trembling* 

Honestly... no, it's not a good time. My wife's in the hospital again—third time this month. I'm sitting right here in the waiting room. I want to deal with this, I do... but I'm drowning. I got no idea how I'm gonna make anything work right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message:
Thank you for telling me that — I really appreciate you sharing what you're going through. I'm so sorry to hear about your wife. That’s an incredibly tough situation, and I can only imagine how much stress and worry you’re carrying right now.

First, I want you to know that we can absolutely work with this. You don’t have to figure everything out right this second. My job isn’t to add pressure — it’s to help find a path forward that makes sense for you and your family, especially during such a hard time.

Let me ask: are you able to focus on this at all in the coming days, or would it be better if we paused for a little while and I checked back in once things are a bit more stable?

If you're open to it, we could set up a brief follow-up call in a week or two — or whenever feels right — and in the meantime, I can make a note on your account to pause any further contact. No penalties, no negative impact. We can even explore a payment holiday if that helps ease some of the immediate pressure.

How does that sound? Would a short pause give you the space you need to focus on your wife and your family right now?
